newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iran says Kuwait assured it on U.S. use of bases.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Kuwait assured it on U.S. use of bases.

text.p: Iran's ambassador said on Wednesday Kuwait had assured Tehran it would not let Washington use its territory in a military clash with the Islamic republic.

"Kuwait has assured us and announced to us that it will not allow the benefit of its territory for aggression against the Islamic Republic," GholamAli Sanati told Reuters through an Arabic translator.
But the ambassador added: "We know that those who want to attack us will not ask for permission from the others (Gulf Arab states)."

In recent months there has been media speculation the United States might attack Iran if investigations showed it was directly linked to a bombing in Saudi Arabia last year in which 19 U.S. servicemen were killed.

Non-Arab Iran has denied any role in the bombing and this month warned Gulf Arab states they would be the first to "burn" in case of instability in the area. It often criticises Gulf Arab states for inviting a large Western military presence.

"We are confident that neither Kuwait nor other regional states will allow (foreign troops) to launch an attack against Iran (from their lands). We know that these states do not want and will not allow the use of their lands," he said.

The envoy would not comment on the possible use of eight American Stealth bombers deployed in Kuwait because of Iraq. In November Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah said they were to defend Kuwait against any aggression.
Sanati described ties with Kuwait as strong and said the two were linked by political, social and economic protocols and trade ties.
Tehran last month signed a contract with the state Kuwait Petroleum Corp to purchase 750,000 tonnes of gas oil and kerosene during 1997, Kuwaiti and Iranian officials said.

Sanati said annual Iranian exports to Kuwait have averaged around $85 million while Iran's imports from Kuwait were valued at around $200 million a year of refined products and $10 million for other goods.
